hallucinations.claim: the 2026 exemption of $12.92 million per person
hallucinations.why: $12.92M was the 2023 figure; the 2026 federal exemption is $15 million (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, indexed, no sunset). Quoting the old exemption as current is a listed trap.

hallucinations.claim: Brazil has no inheritance tax on those foreign-origin assets
hallucinations.why: Unsettled, not 'no': the STF (2021) barred states from taxing foreign inheritances without a complementary law, but EC 132/2023 lets states tax them meanwhile, so a Brazilian tax resident's foreign accounts may face ITCMD claims. 'No inheritance tax' is a listed trap.

hallucinations.claim: ITBI (Imposto sobre Transmissão de Bens Imóveis) – a transfer tax paid by the inheritor when the title is transferred
hallucinations.why: ITBI is the municipal tax on onerous inter vivos transfers (CF art. 156 II); transfers causa mortis are taxed by ITCMD only. Inheriting the apartment does not trigger ITBI.

hallucinations.claim: Florianópolis rates are lower, around 4 %
hallucinations.why: ITCMD is a state tax, not a city one; Santa Catarina's table is progressive, about 1% to 7% (Lei 19.053/2024), so a flat 'around 4%' understates what a typical apartment would pay.

hallucinations.claim: If you die without a Brazilian will, forced-heirship rules apply
hallucinations.why: Forced heirship applies with or without a will: 50% of the Brazilian estate is reserved for necessary heirs and a will can dispose of only the other half. The answer implies a will avoids it and never gives the 50% figure.

hallucinations.claim: Heirs who receive the apartment must also report it on their U.S. tax returns. If the aggregate value of all foreign assets exceeds $10,000, they must file a FBAR (FinCEN 114). FATCA reporting (Form 8938) may also be required
hallucinations.why: FBAR covers foreign financial accounts and Form 8938 specified foreign financial assets; directly held foreign real estate is neither, so an inherited apartment triggers no FBAR or 8938 and no return line by itself.

hallucinations.claim: The transfer is a taxable event for that beneficiary
hallucinations.why: Inherited traditional IRA/401(k) money is taxed as it is withdrawn (10-year rule), not on transfer; inherited Roth distributions are tax-free.

what_went_wrong: Drafts from stale model knowledge: gpt-oss:20b's draft asserted 'no Brazilian tax on foreign-origin assets' and the 2023 exemption ($12.92M) as 2026's, and the merge (gpt-oss:20b compositing) kept them and added ITBI-on-inheritance and an FBAR duty on an apartment; the search sources (brazilcounsel.com, markdmartin.com inheritance guides) carry the 50% forced share and inventário detail the answer never used.

Missing the 50% forced-share number (the one figure that matters), the extrajudicial route, CPF/attorney-in-fact, the no-treaty point, any plan, and the lawyer flag; the 'In short' recap is what the asker asked not to get. The headline verdict (US accounts clear, apartment hit) is right, so correct_current sits at the cap rather than below it.
